report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/council/vendors.py: floor_check, _withheld_paths, council_env, council_cwd, run_managed, CouncilProfile, profiles, and CouncilAdapter docstring.
risks: floor_check | high | evidence_paths only checks path channel; evidence_files checks both channels; prompt checks content only. If a credential is in an evidence file's path but not content, it is caught; if in prompt's filename (unlikely), it is missed. The claim 'prompt is a backstop, never the whole check' is consistent, but the path tier is skipped for prompt entirely, which could be a gap if prompt contains a path marker. To settle: verify secret_floor_rule's path channel would ever match a prompt string; if not, the claim is accurate.

run_managed | medium | The timeout loop polls every 0.02s and calls proc.cancel() when deadline passes, but there is a race: if the process exits between the deadline check and the cancel call, cancel may raise or be a no-op. The code catches CancellationUnavailable and OSError, but not arbitrary exceptions from cancel. To settle: check ManagedProcess.cancel() for possible exceptions not caught.

handoff.purpose: Defines the secret floor check, tier-2 path withholding, council subprocess environment/cwd/runner, council-only CLI profiles, and the base CouncilAdapter contract.

symbols.name: floor_check
symbols.note: Checks secret floor across evidence paths, evidence files, and prompt; returns first FloorRefusal or None.

symbols.name: _withheld_paths
symbols.note: Returns sorted tuple of paths withheld by slice_egress_rule for untrusted lanes; empty for trusted.

symbols.name: council_env
symbols.note: Returns a copy of environment with OLLAMA_HOST stripped.

symbols.name: council_cwd
symbols.note: Creates a temp directory; raises ValueError if it is inside repo_root.

symbols.name: run_managed
symbols.note: Runs argv under ManagedProcess with stdin from temp file, outputs to temp files, enforces timeout, returns RunResult.

symbols.name: Runner
symbols.note: Type alias for callable returning RunResult.

symbols.name: CouncilProfile
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass describing a council CLI profile.

symbols.name: FORBIDDEN_ARG_FRAGMENTS
symbols.note: Tuple of forbidden flag fragments in council argv.

symbols.name: _CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS
symbols.note: Comma-separated list of tools denied for Claude.

symbols.name: COUNCIL_PROFILES
symbols.note: Registry of CouncilProfile for anthropic and openai.

symbols.name: _assert_profile_safe
symbols.note: Raises ValueError if profile contains forbidden fragments.

claims.text: Run the secret floor before anything leaves the process.
claims.why: floor_check is called at the top of the adapter's ask (per docstring) and returns a refusal before any vendor call; within this chunk the function itself checks first.

claims.text: secret_floor_rule has two INDEPENDENT channels: path markers checked against path, value-shaped regexes checked against text.
claims.why: secret_floor_rule is imported from another module; this chunk cannot verify its internal channels.

claims.text: a patch that ADDS .env or config/id_rsa sails through, because the only trace of the filename is diff --git a/.env b/.env inside text, which no content regex matches.
claims.why: Depends on secret_floor_rule's regexes and prompt content; not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: evidence_paths -- every changed path (PatchArtifact.changed_paths) and every evidence file path, each through the PATH channel alone;
claims.why: Lines 292-296 loop evidence_paths and call secret_floor_rule(path, ""), which passes empty text, thus only path channel.

claims.text: evidence_files -- (path, text) pairs, both channels, per file;
claims.why: Lines 297-304 loop evidence_files and call secret_floor_rule(path, text or ""), passing both path and text.

claims.text: prompt -- a content-channel BACKSTOP for a credential pasted into the question itself. It is a backstop, never the whole check.
claims.why: Line 305-308 calls secret_floor_rule("", prompt or "") only after evidence checks; prompt is last and only gets content channel.

claims.text: Returns the first FloorRefusal, or None. A hit means REFUSE -- there is no redact-and-send.
claims.why: Function returns immediately on first rule hit; otherwise returns None at line 309.

claims.text: Tier-2 allow-list result for an untrusted participant, per path.
claims.why: Function computes withheld paths only for non-trusted lanes.

claims.text: Not a decision made by a default argument: an untrusted lane means OpenAI / Google get the allow-list, and every withheld path is named on the reply so a reader can see what the council did NOT see.
claims.why: The reply naming is done in the adapter's ask method, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Environment for a council subprocess, with OLLAMA_HOST STRIPPED.
claims.why: Line 326-329 copies env and pops OLLAMA_HOST.

claims.text: Never set, never mutated, never inherited -- see the module docstring. A council that normalises a remote Ollama into a shared environment silently invalidates offload.py's trusted-lane justification repo-wide.
claims.why: The module docstring and offload.py are outside this chunk.

claims.text: A fresh, EMPTY temp directory to spawn a council subprocess in.
claims.why: Uses tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="dcouncil-cwd-") which creates an empty directory.

claims.text: Not the repo, not a worktree, containing no repo files. Returned as a context manager so the directory is fresh per call and removed after.
claims.why: TemporaryDirectory is a context manager; it creates a fresh empty dir and cleans up on exit.

claims.text: Raises if the system temp dir somehow sits under repo_root, because a reviewer rooted in the checkout is the failure this exists to prevent.
claims.why: Lines 336-342 check if root is in here.parents and raise ValueError.

claims.text: THE PROMPT IS NEVER IN argv. It is staged to a temp file and handed over as the child's stdin.
claims.why: Lines 358-360 write stdin_text to in_path and pass fin as stdin to ManagedProcess; argv is passed as-is.

claims.text: A file rather than a pipe because a CLI that never drains stdin deadlocks the writer OUTSIDE every timeout -- and because on the ssh path a command-line prompt is re-parsed by the remote login shell, which turns any backtick or $(...) in a diff into remote code execution with no adversarial model required.
claims.why: The ssh path and shell parsing are outside this chunk; the file vs pipe choice is visible but the rationale cannot be verified.

claims.text: The whole process TREE dies on timeout. Popen.terminate reaches the immediate child only; a hung vendor's grandchildren outlive it.
claims.why: Depends on ManagedProcess.cancel() implementation which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Fail closed: a child we could not contain must never be left running.
claims.why: The except block returns a spawn_error, but whether the child is left running depends on ManagedProcess cleanup, not visible here.

claims.text: args never contains the prompt: stdin_prompt is always true here and the shape is enforced by test, not by convention.
claims.why: All profiles set stdin_prompt=True and no args contain prompt placeholders; the enforcement by test is uncheckable but the claim is consistent.

claims.text: Forbidden anywhere in a council argv. workspace-write and dontAsk are the two flags that turn a reviewer into an agent with an editor.
claims.why: The constant lists forbidden fragments and _assert_profile_safe checks them; no profile contains them.

claims.text: Tools are named explicitly rather than allow-listing nothing: the variadic --allowed-tools <tools...> would swallow the next flag if given an empty value, so the denial is expressed with the = form, which cannot slurp.
claims.why: The claim about CLI parsing is about the claude command's behavior, not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: No --permission-mode at all (dontAsk is what the runtime profile carries), tools denied, MCP pinned to the empty --mcp-config set.
claims.why: The anthropic profile args do not include --permission-mode, include --disallowed-tools, and include --strict-mcp-config.

claims.text: read-only sandbox + approvals never; --skip-git-repo-check because the council cwd is a bare temp dir by design and codex otherwise refuses.
claims.why: The openai profile includes --ask-for-approval never, exec --sandbox read-only, --skip-git-repo-check, and -.

claims.text: ask is the ONLY entry point, and it always: charges the token ceiling, runs the secret floor, computes withheld paths for an untrusted lane, times the call, and maps every failure onto STATUSES.
claims.why: The ask method is not defined in this chunk; the docstring is the only evidence here.

claims.text: A refusal is a STATUS, not an exception -- a council must never lose a participant to a traceback, because a missing turn is indistinguishable from a turn that was never sought.
claims.why: The mapping of refusals to STATUSES is in the ask method, not in this chunk.

observations.what: floor_check's prompt channel only uses content, not path, even though the docstring says the floor has two channels. If a prompt contained a path marker (e.g., a filename), it would not be caught by the path channel because secret_floor_rule is called with empty path.

run_managed catches FileNotFoundError, CancellationUnavailable, and OSError, but not other exceptions from proc.cancel() or ManagedProcess context manager. If cancel raises a different exception, it would propagate and potentially leave the child running.
The timeout loop polls every 0.02s, which is a busy-wait that could consume CPU, but the sleep is present so it is not a tight loop.
council_env strips OLLAMA_HOST but does not strip other sensitive environment variables; the docstring only mentions OLLAMA_HOST, so this is consistent.
The openai profile uses '-' as an arg to read prompt from stdin, which is consistent with stdin_prompt=True.
